context: Use the existing migration and replacement TODOs as prerequisites. Test from a clean environment with no sibling todo-db checkout and no globally installed CLI. Require package version/lock agreement, wrapper behavior, command parity, rollback evidence, and structural no-duplication checks.
description: Final certification gate after the hosted schema migration, embedded-runtime replacement, package release, and portable shadow tooling. Prove that a clean BenchBox checkout invokes exactly one locked todo-db package, that the wrapper has no legacy fallback, that CI cannot silently bypass the package, and that the duplicate implementation is deleted or restricted to explicitly bounded migration tooling. This is the release gate for claiming canonical runtime ownership.

anti_patterns.dont: Delete the legacy implementation before the canonical package, migration, and canary gates pass
anti_patterns.instead: Keep legacy code outside the default path for a bounded retention window, then remove it in a separate cleanup step
anti_patterns.why: That would remove the only rollback path before the new runtime is proven

anti_patterns.dont: Switch between legacy and canonical databases automatically on command failure
anti_patterns.instead: Require an explicit human rollback decision and a versioned snapshot
anti_patterns.why: Automatic fallback creates split-brain tracker state

anti_patterns.dont: Treat skill-sync verify as proof of runtime behavior
anti_patterns.instead: Run wrapper-level package, migration, audit, and lease-safety gates

preserves.behavior: No automatic legacy fallback between databases
No claim of lease-safety parity until the actual BenchBox wrapper passes the canonical non-holder release test
No generated skill snapshot is committed as a substitute for runtime verification
Rollback is explicit and documented before the first canonical write
The old database and final pre-cutover snapshot remain retained for the approved rollback window

verifications.description: BenchBox scripts dependency is lock-resolved and package version is available
Wrapper integration tests pass against the package runtime
Default wrapper contains no embedded implementation or automatic standalone flag fallback
No production wrapper references the developer-machine standalone checkout
Wrapper rejects package-only destructive recovery commands and preserves exact package export bytes
